The product holds up. Every previously fixed behavior is still fixed, and the deep pass — which the first pass had skipped — exercised bid ingestion with three bidders, hand-recomputed the ADR-0003 math, validated the CSV, awarded and executed an A401, issued an addendum and resolved the out-of-band-low-bid gap. Three claims/safety defects were found and fixed during the audit: sponsor status overclaims, an audit-log dispatch overclaim, and an unflagged absurd low bid. A source-level honesty test plus a unit test guard the fixes.
Residual observations (not defects): the package status badge still reads “RFQs Dispatched” after a zero-delivery dispatch even though the toast and audit event now say no email left the system; OpenAI remains a keyless BYOK adapter; AgentMail free-tier inboxes are reused and disclosed.

New findings

AUD-01MediumSponsor diagnostics overclaimed integration status and registry verification

Repro: open Evals & Architecture → scroll to the sponsor cards. OpenAI showed Integrated / Active with “Primary LLM Reasoning” despite having no API key; Firecrawl claimed “Texas TDLR & TSBPE state contractor licensing registry verification” contradicting the provenance-first discovery behavior; the section header claimed the app “satisfies 100% of the hackathon judging rubric”.

Impact: judges and users read those cards as factual integration/compliance claims; two of them were false.

Fix: cards now read “Adapter Ready / Key Required” (derived from the live provider-availability query), “provenance-first” discovery, accurate AgentMail/free-tier language, and a neutral header. A source-level honesty test now guards these strings. Deployed and re-verified live.

AUD-02MediumAudit log claimed RFQ email dispatch when no email was delivered

Repro: dispatch RFQs on a package whose discovered contacts are all “Contact not published”. The UI toast correctly said no email was delivered, but the audit stream logged “Dispatched invitations to bid to 3 commercial contractor(s) via AgentMail” and the package badge read “RFQs Dispatched”.

Impact: the immutable audit trail — the product’s trust anchor — overstated an outbound action.

Fix: the queueing event is now neutral (“RFQ Invitations Recorded…”), and the dispatch action writes a separate, truthful delivery event with real counts and per-recipient reasons. Verified live: “AgentMail Delivery: 0 of 0 eligible recipient(s)” + reasons for all three contacts.

Residual (product call): the package status badge still reads “RFQs Dispatched” after zero delivery; recommend a “queued / delivery failed” indicator or renaming the status.

AUD-03InfoGuarded action failures log a client console error

Observation: when a user triggers an action the backend intentionally rejects (zero-recipient dispatch), Convex logs a server error in the browser console while the UI shows the error toast. This is expected for a thrown action but will appear as a console error to anyone auditing. No fix applied; documented so the next auditor does not report it as a new defect.

AUD-04MediumAn absurd lowball bid was ranked #1 with no sanity warning

Repro (deep pass): on a fresh fixture with a $1,250,000 Division 26 package, ingest a proposal with “Base Bid Price: $250,000.00 — everything included”. The bid is accepted by the plausibility floor, stored at $250,000, ranked #1 “Best Leveled Value”, and the matrix showed no flag or warning. The only guard in place is the <$1,000 / >5× budget rejection.

Impact: an omitted-scope or mis-read bid can be awarded as the compliant winner with no friction.

Fix: new getSuspiciouslyLowBidIds() flags any bid whose leveled cost is below 50% of the package budget. The matrix shows an “Out-of-Band Low Bid — Verify Before Awarding” banner when the leader is flagged and a “Verify — unusually low” chip per card/column. Non-blocking by design; verified live (banner and chip both render) and unit-tested.

AUD-05Clarified“Adjust Leveling” appeared enabled after execution

Observation that triggered it: after execution, a scan of buttons matching /Adjust Leveling/ found controls that were not disabled. Deeper inspection showed the executed bid's control is relabelled “Leveling Locked” and bound to disabled={isBidAgreementExecuted(bid._id)}; the matches were the other (non-awarded) bids' controls, which correctly remain adjustable. Not a defect — recorded so the next auditor applies per-card checks rather than a global regex.

Method notes for future auditors. (1) Chrome’s innerText applies CSS text-transform: the holdout label renders as “HOLDOUT — ANSWER NOT IN PROMPT”, so case-sensitive string checks fail even though the card is visible. (2) A programmatic element.click() does not move focus, so focus-restore checks must use a real mouse click or an explicit focus. (3) Guarded action failures (e.g., zero-recipient RFQ dispatch) intentionally log a client console error from the thrown Convex action; the UI converts it into a visible error toast.

Honest self-interrogation

QuestionAnswer
Is every known-state row re-verified with evidence?Yes — 25 verified pass, 2 initially flagged and then clarified as method artifacts (holdout card rendering under CSS uppercase; focus restore after a programmatic click). Neither is an app defect.
Did I reproduce every new finding twice?The sponsor overclaim and the dispatch overclaim were each observed in two independent runs (Phase A screenshot + backend read; Phase C backend read + direct action run) before being fixed.
Did I test realtime with two contexts and measure latency?Yes — independent browser contexts; the RFI appeared in context B 1.0 s after context A (1 s polling granularity, effectively push).
Did I reconcile numbers against the backend?Yes — 9 values checked against Convex queries; all agreed (buyout 3,918,500; gaps 186,000; award 1/3; contract 1,225,000; LD 1,200; counts 3/4/3/2/4; holdout 3/3).
Did I fix things instead of only reporting them?Yes — both new claims-integrity findings were fixed, deployed and re-verified live: sponsor card wording (with a source test) and the audit delivery log (verified: “AgentMail Delivery: 0 of 0 eligible recipient(s)” with reasons).
What could still be wrong in this report?The agent journeys cover two goals, not every persona end-to-end; file upload/a11y checks are deterministic-harness checks, not agent-driven. The random Firecrawl results mean discovery content varies between runs. The residual “RFQs Dispatched” badge after zero delivery is a product call.
